blocks.x: How IoT, Twin & Robotics lands in Capabilities — the constraints that shape the build, the gated delivery pattern, and the deltas we commit against your baseline.

In Logistics & Supply Chain, iot, digital twin & robotics bridges the physical and digital enterprise: industrial sensor network, digital twin platforms, computer vision and edge ai, predictive maintenance, robotics and autonomous systems integration, connected products, and smart infrastructure. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: industrial iot & sensor network, digital twin platform engineering, computer vision & edge ai — delivered on Dataq Twinverse and Dataq Nexus with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Fleet and yard telemetry gaps
Trailer/container/yard assets lack sensing; detention, dwell and theft are discovered in invoices. Cold-chain excursions surface at claim time.
Visibility stitched from portals
Carrier portals, EDI and telematics produce a patchwork; the control tower reads yesterday. Exceptions surface as customer complaints.
Dispatch and exception work manual
Planners re-plan routes and loads by hand when trucks break down or orders change; exception queues eat capacity that should improve the network.

blocks.x: How we deliver it in this sector

Delivery composes 7 services from the IoT, Digital Twin & Robotics tower — Industrial IoT & sensor network, Digital Twin Platform Engineering, Computer Vision & Edge AI, Predictive Maintenance & Asset Intelligence as the usual core — sequenced through the Dataq Method, with CSRD/ISSB logistics emissions obligations shaping the design from the first sprint.
Services we deploy in this sector

items: Industrial IoT & Sensor Fabric
Sense everything that matters: retrofit-friendly sensor network with governed telemetry.
Digital Twin Platform Engineering
Simulate before you cut steel: plant, fleet and product twins with governed physics and data.
Computer Vision & Edge AI
Cameras into instruments: inspection, safety and counting at the edge, inside policy.
Predictive Maintenance & Asset Intelligence
Fix it before it fails: RUL models wired into planning, spare parts and work orders.
Fleet and trailer sensing
Telematics, door and temperature telemetry with governance (cold-chain and detention visible live)
Yard and dock orchestration
Gate, yard and dock telemetry into appointment systems (dwell time down 25-40%)
Exception resolution time
Hours instead of days via agentic remediation
Cold-chain excursions
Intercepted in transit, not at claims
On-time-in-full
Up 5-10 points on orchestrated lanes

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: CSRD/ISSB logistics emissions and CSRD/ISSB logistics emissions. Scope 3 transport emissions with auditability. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

A fixed rhythm keeps progress visible from week one — here is the one we run. The first two weeks lock the baseline: your team and ours measure the current metric together and sign it. Weeks 3–8 carry the pilot on bounded scope — a single decision path, workflow, plant or portfolio — and a control owner on your side owns the evidence. Weeks 9–12 industrialize: runbooks, monitoring, enablement, and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Missing a gate produces a documented decision to stop or redirect — never a silent extension.
